newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-FEYENOORD FANCY CHANCES AGAINST TROUBLED AJAX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FEYENOORD FANCY CHANCES AGAINST TROUBLED AJAX.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam, facing an early exit from the European Cup, must switch their focus back to the league on Sunday for a highly-charged away clash with rivals Feyenoord.
As if meeting an in-form Feyenoord in a hostile Rotterdam stadium were not enough, Ajax coach Louis van Gaal has half a side missing through injury and problems mounting by the day.

Van Gaal, who has used 23 players in five Champions' league matches, will be without key defenders Danny Blind and Frank de Boer, midfield pivots Jari Litmanen and Richard Witschge as well as Peter Hoekstra and Kiki Musampa.

With Van Gaal himself leaving the club at the end of the season, Marc Overmars and striker Patrick Kluivert mulling their futures and Ronald de Boer quoted in the media as saying he prefers playing for his country than for his club, the current world champions look to be in dire straits and ill-prepared for a crucial league encounter.
The injury crisis and the transfer of players to the more lucrative southern European leagues have hit dressing-room morale and confidence has plummeted.
Ajax languish sixth in the league, nine points behind leaders PSV Eindhoven and eight adrift of Feyenoord. The two clubs' European exploits midweek encapsulated their contrasting fortunes.
Feyenoord look well set to progress to the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup, while Ajax's gloom deepened with a second home Champions' league defeat to unfancied French side Auxerre.

Ajax face the real prospect of going into the mid-winter break out of Europe and out of contention in the league, hoping only to qualify for next season's UEFA Cup and keep their increasingly disenchanted fans flocking to the costly new space-age Arena stadium.
In contrast, Feyenoord, the first Dutch club to capture the European Cup in 1970, the year before Ajax won the first of three back-to-back titles, are set fair after re-building in the summer.
Coach Arie Haan has settled his side into a 4-4-2 formation, with Ronald Koeman the lynchpin in his last season before retiring.

For the first time in four seasons Feyenoord are clear favourites to win the game, one of the classics in the Dutch soccer calendar, although Ajax can point to the history books which show they have won the last five games in Rotterdam.
The Amsterdam side did the double over their rivals last season, coming from 2-0 down to win 4-2 in Rotterdam and winning 2-0 at home.
While Ajax plunder the reserve team to field a full side, Haan can draw on almost a full squad for Sunday's clash.
Haan was doubly pleased after Tuesday's UEFA Cup third round first-leg trip to Tenerife -- a goalless draw which sets them up nicely for the return and no injuries.
Argentine defender Patricio Graff is suspended and midfielder Jean-Paul van Gastel is out with a broken leg but defender George Boateng returns from suspension.

Such is the bitter rivalry between the two camps that Rotterdam mayor Bram Peper has called for the game to be moved from an evening kick-off to the afternoon so that up to 400 police can control fans during daylight hours.
Six years ago, a teenage Feyenoord fan was jailed for hurling a home-made bomb which injured over a dozen rival fans at an Ajax-Feyenoord game.
Possible teams:
Feyenoord: Ed de Goey, George Boateng, Geoffrey Claeys, Henk Fraser, Ronald Koeman, Bernard Schuiteman; Kees van Wonderen, Giovanni van Bronckhorst, Pablo Sanchez, Gaston Taument, Henryk Larsson.
Ajax Amsterdam: Edwin van der Sar, Santos, Winston Bogarde, Mario Melchiot, Menno Willems, Ronald de Boer, Arnold Scholten, Nordin Wooter, Tijani Babangida, Marc Overmars, Patrick Kluivert.
